summary: Hosakote Krishna Sastri (1870–1928) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India as Assistant Superintendent for Epigraphy (~1891–1925) and Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925), and also lectured at the University of Calcutta.

Hoseok Leigh is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. Leigh studied under teacher Ha-u Kim and earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoseong Kim is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo. He held a professorship at Dongguk University (attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara (1928–2008) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served on the faculty at Koyasan University, where he was a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2004).

Hoyo Watanabe (1933–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1956). He spent his academic career at Rissho University as a professor (~1974–2004) and Dean of Buddhist Studies (attested 1984–1985).
Hozen Seki (1903–1991) was an American Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy. He served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian (1876–1953) was a linguist who studied at Paris, Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1897–1898), and under Antoine Meillet (1902). He taught at the Aramiyan School (1893), Sanasarian College (1894), and Yerevan State University (1923).

Hsiao-Lan Hu is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Temple University. Hu served as associate professor of Religious Studies & Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) was a Buddhist leader and scholar who studied under Zhikai, Ruoshun, and Yin Shun. He founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as abbot (~1967–1985), and held posts at Chinese Culture, Tunghai, and Nanjing universities.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fo Guang University (attested 2009), earning a master's degree under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist monk and scholar who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953 and served as its honorary president.

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Chang Zhi (~1937) and Hsu Yun (1948). He founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, serving as abbot (~1976–1995), and established the Buddhist Text Translation Society.
Hsueh-li Cheng (1939–2020) was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ohio University (~1974–1977) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1977–2020).

Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology, studying under Huanxian Yuan. He taught at the Republic of China Military Academy, Chinese Culture University (~1963), National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

Huaiyu Chen (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and completed a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, later becoming assistant professor at Arizona State University (~2008).

Huanhuan He specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the University of Tokyo (attested 2015), and as a professor at Zhejiang University (attested 2015).
Huawen Bai (1930–2021) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1951–1955), he served as a professor there from approximately 1955 to 2000.

Hubert Decleer (1940–2021) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte (1975). He served as academic director (1987) and senior faculty advisor (1999) at the School for International Training.

Hubert Durt (1936–2018) studied Buddhist studies under Étienne Lamotte (~1958–1965). He served as director of the Hōbōgirin Institute and professor at École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1970–2001), and later as professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2001–2012).
